command.simpleclouds.weather.override:
Simple Clouds is overriding vanilla weather, and the /weather command is disabled. To use vanilla weather, please do either of the following:
1. Set the cloud mode in the SERVER config to AMBIENT.
2. Set the cloud mode in the SERVER config to SINGLE, and set the single mode cloud type to a cloud type that has no weather associated with it (e.x. simpleclouds:itty_bitty)

gui.simpleclouds.config.client.option.cl:
Specifies how the clouds should behave in a client-side only context. SINGLE uses only a single cloud type. AMBIENT carves clouds around the player, keeping them at a distance. Due to be on a client-side only context, DEFAULT can not be picked and the vanilla weather system will be used. If Simple Clouds is installed on a server, this option will be ignored and the client will instead use the option set by the server.
Default: AMBIENT
Allowed Values: SINGLE, AMBIENT
gui.simpleclouds.config.client.option.de:
Toggles the generation of the cloud mesh.
Default: true

Toggles rendering of the clouds.
Default: true
gui.simpleclouds.config.client.option.di: Specifies the allowed dimensions that Simple Clouds is active in Allowed values: minecraft:dimension.

Toggles cloud shadows cast onto terrain, including nearby terrain under overhead clouds and distant terrain when available.
Default: true

Specifies the distance cloud shadows can render across terrain.
Default: 4096
 Default: 4096

gui.simpleclouds.config.client.option.pe:
Culls cloud chunks not visible to the player. Generally should not be disabled, but can fix visual issues when looking around fast with higher frames per mesh generation values.
Default: true
Frustum Culling

Specifies the quality of the level of detail. A lower setting makes clouds lower quality faster.
Default: HIGH
Allowed Values: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH
Level Of Detail

Specifies how many frames it should take to generate the entire cloud mesh. Higher values will improve performance at the cost of stuttery cloud movement.
Default: 1
 Default: 1
 Range: 1 ~ 30
Frames To Generate Mesh

How the amount of frames used to generate the entire mesh is calculated. Static will use the 'Frames To Generate Mesh' option. Dynamic will calculate it automatically depending on your FPS. Target FPS will target a certain perceived framerate for mesh generation.
Default: TARGET_FPS
Allowed Values: STATIC, DYNAMIC, TARGET_FPS
Generation Interval

Used to set the target FPS with the 'Target FPS' option in 'Generation Interval'.
Default: 24
 Default: 24
 Range: 1 ~ 480
Target Mesh Gen Fps

Specifies if distant level-of-detail cloud chunks should be rendered. Disabling can improve performance, but removes faraway cloud coverage.
Default: true
Render Lod Clouds

Specifies if 'rain' beneath storm clouds should appear or not. Disabling can improve performance, especially when in VR.
Default: true
Render Storm Fog

Toggles lightning flashes that can be seen in storm fog. Disabling can lead to potential performance gains when lightning spawns.
Default: true
Storm Fog Lightning Flashes

Specifies if faces that are not visible to the camera should be tested during mesh generation. Settings this to off can improve performance at the cost of visual issues with shadows and storm fog.
Default: true
Test Sides That Are Occluded

Legacy option retained for config compatibility. The opaque-only renderer ignores transparent cube distance.
Default: 50
 Default: 50
 Range: 1 ~ 100
Transparency Render Distance Percentage

gui.simpleclouds.error.couldNotLoadMeshS:
Failed to load the mesh compute shader. Please make a bug report on the mod's GitHub repository, linked below. Make sure to include the crash report and latest.log file with your issue.

To developers: If you are modifying the cube_mesh.comp file using a resource pack and have made an error, this message will appear on start up. Please see the latest.log for more details.
gui.simpleclouds.error.opengl:
The currently selected display adapter does not support Simple Clouds.

Simple Clouds only supports display adapters that have OpenGL 4.3+ capabilities.

Please make sure:
1. Your drivers are up to date
2. You are not using integrated graphics instead of a discrete GPU to run Minecraft.

If you are a MacOS user, Simple Clouds IS NOT SUPPORTED as the OS is stuck on OpenGL 4.1. Unfortunately, this is a limitation that Simple Clouds cannot work around.

simpleclouds.config.preset.high.descript: Restores the fuller Simple Clouds presentation with high detail, distant cloud coverage, storm fog, and terrain shadows enabled.
simpleclouds.config.preset.low.descripti: Cuts distant cloud coverage and some extra visual features for weaker systems while keeping clouds visible.
simpleclouds.config.preset.medium.descri: Balances visuals and performance by lowering level of detail slightly and slowing mesh generation a bit.
simpleclouds.config.preset.off.descripti: Disables Simple Clouds visuals for this player, including cloud rendering, storm fog, and atmospheric cloud layers.
